summary: Implemented the one endpoint this task owns, POST /api/v1/contracts/third-party-paper, on the Python/FastAPI/PostgreSQL stack CLAUDE.md specifies, reusing the foundation task's `uploaded_files` ORM model and the clauses/contracts tasks' router/service/repository layering and auth/db/error infrastructure unchanged. Added app/schemas/file_upload.py (UploadThirdPartyPaperRequest, FileUploadResponse matching context.json field-for-field, camelCase), app/repositories/files.py (insert_uploaded_file -- data access only), app/services/files.py (format validation reproducing UC2-AF-005's exact message, size validation reproducing UC2-AF-006's exact message, a base64-content sanity check, and persistence to `uploaded_files`), and a new app/routers/contracts_third_party_paper.py wired into app/main.py as its own router rather than editing app/routers/contracts.py, which T-CONTRACTS-API already owns and completed -- per CLAUDE.md's module-addition rule this task adds a handler alongside existing ones instead of touching another task's file. UC2-BR-008 (Template/Upload mutual exclusivity) and UC2-MF-001's full create flow are UI-state and already-implemented-elsewhere behavior respectively (POST /api/v1/contracts, built by T-CONTRACTS-API, already validates Template/third-party-paper mutual exclusivity and resolves thirdPartyPaperFileId against this task's `uploaded_files` table) -- this task's own surface is the upload call itself, which has no templateId concept to cross-check against. Added 9 tests (tests/test_contracts_third_party_paper.py): the role matrix (401/403), happy path for both permitted roles with field-by-field FileUploadResponse assertions, the exact-message rejections for unsupported format (UC2-AF-005) and oversized file (UC2-AF-006), a boundary test at exactly 25 MB, a reject-then-successful-reupload sequence, and an invalid-base64-content rejection. `python -m compileall app` and `pytest -q` both pass (77/77, including the pre-existing 68). Verified live against uvicorn: the route appears in /openapi.json with the right method, request/response schemas and the X-User-Role/X-User-Id security schemes, and the 401/403 role-matrix behaves correctly end-to-end without a database (role/tenant resolution happens before any DB dependency runs). Could not verify the DB-backed 201/400 paths against a live server -- this sandbox has no reachable Postgres (connection to localhost:5432 refused), the same gap T-CLAUSES-API and T-CONTRACTS-API already documented -- that behavior is instead proven by the 9-test TestClient suite against an in-memory SQLite session through the identical get_db/current_tenant_id dependency chain production uses. Killed the server when done.

code_files.description: UploadThirdPartyPaperRequest, FileUploadResponse -- camelCase fields matching context.json exactly. fileFormat is typed str (not Literal['PDF','DOCX']) so the business-rule layer in app/services/files.py can reproduce UC2-AF-005's exact message on an unsupported value instead of a generic Pydantic validation error.
insert_uploaded_file -- the only data-access operation this endpoint needs. No business rules.

Business rules: format validation (UC2-AF-005's exact 'Unsupported file format. Please upload PDF or DOCX only.'), size validation against the 25 MB limit (UC2-AF-006's exact 'File size exceeds the 25 MB limit. Please upload a smaller file.'), a base64-content sanity check, server-side id generation, and persistence of an `uploaded_files` row with a derived storageUrl.

Thin HTTP binding for POST /api/v1/contracts/third-party-paper with require_roles('TENANT_ADMIN','CONTRACT_OWNER') exactly as named in the endpoint table. A new file, not an edit to app/routers/contracts.py (owned by the already-completed T-CONTRACTS-API task), per CLAUDE.md's module-addition rule.
Modified: registered app.routers.contracts_third_party_paper.router under the /api/v1 prefix, alongside the existing clauses/contracts routers.

9 tests: role matrix (401 missing header, 403 disallowed role), happy path for both permitted roles with full FileUploadResponse field assertions, UC2-AF-005's exact rejection message, UC2-AF-006's exact rejection message, the 25 MB boundary (accepted at exactly the limit), a reject-then-successful-reupload sequence, and an invalid-base64-content rejection.

pr.title: feat(uc123): contracts third-party-paper upload endpoint
pr.body: Implements T-CONTRACTS-THIRD-PARTY-PAPER-API: POST /api/v1/contracts/third-party-paper. Adds a dedicated files router/service/repository layer reusing the foundation task's uploaded_files model and the clauses/contracts tasks' auth/db/error infrastructure unchanged. See blockers for judgement calls: fileFormat validated as a business rule rather than a DTO enum to preserve exact story message text, a derived storageUrl in the absence of any configured object-storage dependency, an added base64-content sanity check, no Location header (no GET-by-id endpoint exists for this resource in the contract), and a sandbox verification gap with no reachable Postgres.

blockers: context.json marks UploadThirdPartyPaperRequest.fileFormat and FileUploadResponse.fileFormat as an enum (PDF, DOCX). I kept the Pydantic field typed `str` rather than `Literal['PDF','DOCX']`: UC2-AF-005 names an exact user-facing message ('Unsupported file format. Please upload PDF or DOCX only.') for an unsupported value, and a Pydantic Literal would instead reject the request during shape validation and surface the shared generic `{"error": "validation failed", ...}` body. I validate the value as a business rule in app/services/files.py instead, which reproduces the story's exact copy -- the same precedent T-CONTRACTS-API's blockers already documented for conditionally-required fields. The value is normalized to upper case before being persisted/returned, so the response still only ever contains 'PDF' or 'DOCX'.

FileUploadResponse.storageUrl is required (nullable:false) but no story or DTO field describes an actual object-storage backend, and CLAUDE.md's Dependencies section forbids adding a new package (e.g. an S3/blob-storage client) beyond what the manifest already declares. I persist the uploaded file's metadata (name/size/format) to the existing `uploaded_files` table and derive storageUrl as a deterministic path reference by the generated file id (`/files/{fileId}`) -- the raw base64 bytes themselves are not written to any blob store, since none is configured in this repo. A future task that adds real object storage would only need to change how storageUrl is produced, not this endpoint's contract.

Added one check beyond context.json's explicit fields: fileContentBase64 is validated as decodable base64, rejecting with a 400 if it is not. No story names this exact scenario, but UC2-MF-001's 'the system validates the file type and size and attaches it' implies the uploaded content itself is usable, and a non-base64 payload cannot be attached to anything downstream. This is a minimal addition, not a new DTO field.

No `Location` response header is set on the 201, unlike this module's other create endpoints (contracts, clauses): this contract defines no GET-by-id endpoint for an uploaded file (no `/api/v1/files/{id}` route in any task's endpoint table), so there is no URI to point Location at. The response body's `fileId` is the only way a caller can reference the upload afterward (e.g. as CreateContractRequest.thirdPartyPaperFileId).

UC2-BR-008 (Template/Upload Third Party Paper mutual exclusivity) and most of UC2-MF-001's acceptance criteria describe UI state (disabling the Template dropdown, loading a template preview, counterparty search results, etc.) that this task's single upload endpoint has no surface to enforce or express -- this endpoint neither knows nor is told whether a Template is currently selected. The actual mutual-exclusivity and document-source validation happens at contract-creation time, in POST /api/v1/contracts (T-CONTRACTS-API, already implemented), which rejects a request carrying both templateId and thirdPartyPaperFileId and resolves a given thirdPartyPaperFileId against this task's `uploaded_files` table. This task's own contribution to those stories is limited to producing a valid, persisted upload for that later validation to reference.

Sandbox has no reachable Postgres (connection to localhost:5432 refused), the same gap T-CLAUSES-API and T-CONTRACTS-API already documented. Verified instead: (1) the route appears in /openapi.json with the right method, request/response schemas and security schemes via a live uvicorn boot; (2) the 401/403 role-matrix live, end-to-end, with no database at all (role/tenant resolution runs before any DB dependency resolves); (3) every DB-backed behavior -- happy path for both roles, exact-message format/size rejections, the 25 MB boundary, and the reject-then-reupload sequence -- through tests/test_contracts_third_party_paper.py's 9 tests against a real FastAPI TestClient wired to an in-memory SQLite session through the identical get_db/current_tenant_id dependency chain production uses.
